title: 7 Cool Cars We’d Rock in Grand Theft Auto VI

body_markdown: Say what you want about the criminal behavior modeled in the *Grand Theft Auto* video games, but the long-awaited sixth installment is an incredibly detailed game that is both stupendously popular and critically acclaimed. First-day sales totaled $3.79 billion, according to its publisher Take-Two Interactive, and the game earned a nearly perfect score of 99 on[Metacritic](https://www.metacritic.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi/) —the highest score the site has ever given. *GTA VI* is remarkably lifelike not only because of how big the world is—closely modeled on Miami and the Florida Keys—but also because of how the game plays. You don’t just break into cars and run drugs; you also fix up your house, buy your girlfriend jewelry, and console your grieving friend by taking him fishing. Your car can run out of gas, and when you smash into street signs, you must pay to fix the damage to your vehicle. Speaking of smashing into things, driving in this game is surprisingly difficult: You’re not simply navigating traffic but controlling your vehicle, which pitches and rolls and dives and reacts differently on different surfaces. Realistic? Definitely. Challenging? That, too. Our favorite part of the game, of course, is the cars. Yes, you do get very good at stealing them, but the various vehicles of *GTA VI* aren’t simply there to be stolen. They’re there to complete the world, and they aren’t neatly divided between “cool stuff” and “generic boringmobiles.” There are cars old and new, plus semis and pickup trucks and flatbeds and box trucks and UTVs, not to mention boats, bikes, planes, construction vehicles, and even pizza-delivery vans. A “Pfister Growler” parked in the handicap spot of a pizza joint on Key Lento. Pfister owners, amirite? Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games If the names of each vehicle below read like nonsense, and each one looks like an obvious knockoff, you’re partially correct. The game’s developers didn’t license official versions of the vehicles they are clearly ripping off, because no self-respecting OEM is going to willingly associate itself with (virtual) crime. Therefore, it can’t use the “real” names of the “fake” cars. The names aren’t quite nonsense, though. Look closely, and the naming convention reveals itself as a series of inside jokes written by people fluent in automotive culture and with ready access to middle-school-level crass humor. Below are seven of our favorites after having dedicated a few hours (okay, maybe a little more than that) to the game since it debute last week. We’re sure there are plenty more we’ll discover as we get further in. ## ’70 Vapid Ganado Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games This is the vehicle you see the most in the beginning of the game, because the ute belongs to one of the main characters, 30-year-old Jason Duval. Heavily patinaed at the beginning, in shades of green and blue, your friend Joey at Coastal Auto Care shop offers a free respray along with new rod bearings. You accept, because your girlfriend will appreciate it. (A rather superficial judgment, if you ask me.) Knowing that ’70s and brown go together like winter mornings and chai, we chose a fetching shade of chocolate. The name “Ganado” means livestock or cattle in Spanish, a nod to the real identity of this car-truck hybrid: The fourth-gen Ford Ranchero. It’s an appropriate choice for Jason: American, under the radar, showing the results of a hard life, ready for action. Whoever established “Vapid” as the moniker for “Ford” clearly had a bone to pick with the Blue Oval, though … ## Imponte Phoenix Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games The Imponte Phoenix is a second-gen Pontiac Firebird Trans Am, complete with “screaming chicken” hood decal. (Unfortunately, said thunderchicken gets painted over in a quick respray to help you avoid the law after you ** “release” it from “captivity” in a police impound lot.) Check out the snowflake wheels! We did rock this car, albeit briefly, but since we liberated it on behalf of our boss, who needed us to liberate some … leafy greens from its trunk, we couldn’t keep it. Bummer. ## Vapid Caracara 4×4 Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games This F-150 Raptor (probably the R version, with the V-8) lookalike belongs to Brian Heder, your totally HR-compliant boss and distributor of non-addictive substances, who gives you entirely legal jobs to do that don’t involve any crime whatsoever. He owns your house, which he’s letting you rent for free, as long as you do all the maintenance. He’s so nice! This menacing trophy-truck-for-the-streets makes lots of sense for Brian, especially as a pursuit vehicle, as he seeks to peacefully resolve a simple misunderstanding with his long-time colleague Arnold that involves zero off-road driving and no firearms. Listen, no one said it was illegal to leap across gaps in a broken bridge. That’s just outdoor recreation in the Keys! The name of this truck refers to a type of long-legged hawk in North America that falls into the falcon family. Falcons, in case you hadn’t brushed up on your avian taxonomy lately, are a type of raptor. According to Wikipedia, “Caracaras are territorial creatures who are year-round landlords of trees and land that they occupy.” Kinda describes Brian, if you think of it. ## ’67 Sirius Transgressor Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games We were particularly interested in the Classic Car Collection side-mission, available in the Ultimate Edition of *GTA VI* along with an edition-exclusive car we’ll discuss next. Not new to the world of video games but a first for the *GTA* franchise, this mission (in Chapter Two) is exactly what it sounds like: Searching for and finding abandoned old cars that need some TLC, and working with a shop to restore them to glory. As it might happen in the real world, you bump into a mechanic named Wyman at a motel pool. After you help him fix his ’67 Vapid Dominator (a rally-build first-gen Mustang), he asks for help restoring other vintage cars. Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games The mission involves finding restoration candidates and “scanning” multiple examples of the same model—the game’s version of finding parts cars. This Mercury Cougar knock-off is the first of five potential restoration candidates, including a Riata (a first-gen Bronco wearing period-incorrect Free Wheeling stripes) and a Mamba GT (a Daytona Coupe lookalike). Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games ## 1955 Vapid Stanier Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games Exclusive to the Ultimate Edition of *GTA VI* , the ’55 Vapid Stanier parked outside the Boardwalk Hotel (and not available until Chapter 3) is a mish-mash of ’50s cars. Vapid translates to Ford in *GTA* -parlance, so it owes much to the ’55 Fairlane, but we’re detecting some Buick Roadmaster in the side treatment and some Packard in the headlights. This car is not just a reference to 1950s automotive history (as viewed through a prism). It’s also a reference to *Grand Theft Auto: Vice City* (2002), in which an “Oceanic” is parked outside the Ocean View Hotel, and a nod to real life: A yellow-and-white Oldsmobile Super 88 sits outside the Avalon Hotel on Ocean Drive, Miami Beach. The references in the *GTA* franchise are hardly the only ones to this real-life car and hotel. Per Avalon Hotel’s website: “The bright-yellow 1955 Oldsmobile Super 88 convertible parked in front of the Avalon has the distinction of being one of the most photographed cars in America, enthralling locals and tourists alike. We have served as the backdrop for many photoshoots and films, including *Scarface* , *Miami Vice* , *Bad Boys 3* , and Sidney Pollack’s *Random Hearts* .” ## Maibatsu Penumbra Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games This is perhaps the coolest car we found thus far in *GTA 6* : A Maibatsu Penumbra, aka Mitsubishi Eclipse, modeled after the 1995 example driven by Brian O’Conner in *The Fast and the Furious* . Penumbra, taken almost directly from Latin words meaning “almost” and “shadow,” is “a space of partial illumination (as in an eclipse) between the perfect shadow on all sides and the full light.”[Fast and Furious fans](https://www.hagerty.com/media/buying-and-selling/auctions/the-7-most-expensive-fast-furious-movie-cars-ever-sold/) will recognize the green Eclipse as the first car that Brian races (unsuccessfully) against Dom. Remember “Warning!!! Danger to Manifold?” Same scene. ## Albany Emperor Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games The one quality missing from the other cars on this list is a sense of luxury. This variation on downsized, Broughamy Cadillacs of the late ’70s balances luxury with that under-the-radar vibe that all, erm, respectable businesspeople value. The only potential drawback of this classy ride is its lack of off-road performance—and if you’ve explored the *GTA* world at all, you’ll know that various excursions—such as chasing and destroying an ambulance, to take a totally random example—take you off-road. If we were annoyed by the off-roadability of a Ford Expedition (and we were), this kinda-Caddy wouldn’t be much better. This sort-of Nissan Patrol, on the other hand, would be excellent: Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games When we’re established in our career, perhaps we’ll return to this as an around-town car. Of course, should we prefer to display our success with more flash, there are plenty of options from Pfister (Porsche), such as this not-a-Taycan. Take-Two Interactive / Rockstar Games Or we could go the Italian route, with this not-a-Lamborghini. We’re not entirely sure which model this “Pegassi” replicates—we’re seeing Aventador but also Gallardo? Flip through the gallery below to enjoy a smattering of fun vehicles from the game that’s the talk of any town with an internet connection and a PS5.
